question: The Rajya Sabha is to the Union Government as the ________ is to the State Government. (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Governor's Office
Chief Minister's Office
State Legislative Council
State Legislative Assembly
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is State Legislative Council

Explanation:
The State Legislative Council plays the same role for the state government as the Rajya Sabha does for the Union government. Both are the upper houses or second chambers of the legislature. The Legislative Council is the upper house of the state legislature while the Legislative Assembly is the lower house. At the centre, the Rajya Sabha is the upper house, which is indirectly elected. Similarly, the Legislative Council is also indirectly elected and reviews bills passed by the Legislative Assembly. It ensures bicameralism in the legislature. The Governor's office or Chief Minister's office are not legislative houses but executive positions.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Who is the Chairman of Rajya Sabha? → Vice President
☛ Who is the Chairman of the Legislative Council? → Chairman appointed by the Governor
☛ How many states have a bicameral legislature? → 6 states
☛ What is the minimum number of members in a Legislative Council? → 40
☛ How are members of the Legislative Council elected? → Indirectly
question_hi: राज्य सरकार के लिए विधान परिषद वही है जो केंद्र सरकार के लिए ________ है। (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: राज्यपाल का कार्यालय
मुख्यमंत्री का कार्यालय
राज्य विधान परिषद
राज्य विधान सभा
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है राज्य विधान परिषद

Explanation:
राज्य सरकार के लिए विधान परिषद वही भूमिका निभाती है जो केंद्र सरकार के लिए राज्यसभा निभाती है। दोनों ही द्वितीय सदन या उच्च सदन हैं। विधान परिषद राज्य विधानमंडल का ऊपरी सदन है जबकि विधान सभा निचला सदन है। केंद्र में राज्यसभा उच्च सदन है, जो अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से निर्वाचित होती है। इसी प्रकार, विधान परिषद भी अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से निर्वाचित होती है और विधान सभा द्वारा पारित विधेयकों की समीक्षा करती है। यह विधानमंडल में द्विसदनीयता का प्रावधान सुनिश्चित करती है। राज्यपाल का कार्यालय या मुख्यमंत्री का कार्यालय विधायी सदन नहीं हैं, बल्कि कार्यकारी पद हैं।

question: In October 2024, the Supreme Court by what majority upheld constitutional validity of Section 6A of the Citizenship Act? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: 3 : 2
8 : 1
4 : 1
5 : 2
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 4 : 1

Explanation:
In October 2024, a 5-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court upheld the constitutional validity of Section 6A of the Citizenship Act, 1955 by a 4:1 majority. This section is linked to the Assam Accord (1985) and grants citizenship to migrants who entered Assam between 1 January 1966 and 25 March 1971. Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud authored the majority opinion, while Justice Pardiwala dissented. The Court held that the section balances demographic security and humanitarian concerns of Assam.

☛ When was the Assam Accord signed? → 1985
☛ Cut-off date for citizenship under Section 6A? → 25 March 1971
☛ How many judges were on the bench? → 5
☛ Which judge dissented? → Justice Pardiwala

question: The idea of a 'welfare state' is promoted by which of the following with respect to the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Fundamental Duties
Directive Principles of State Policy
Preamble
Fundamental Rights
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Directive Principles of State Policy

Explanation:
The idea of a 'welfare state' in the Indian Constitution is primarily promoted through the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV, Articles 36-51). These principles direct the government to formulate policies and enact laws to achieve social and economic justice. They are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by courts, but are fundamental in the governance of the country. They include provisions such as equal pay for equal work, right to education, and public health. The Preamble also mentions a welfare state, but its detailed implementation is through the Directive Principles.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which part of the Indian Constitution contains Directive Principles? → Part IV
☛ Directive Principles are inspired by the Constitution of which country? → Ireland
☛ What does a welfare state mean? → Government intervention for citizens' welfare
☛ Which Article deals with equal pay for equal work? → Article 39(d)
☛ Are Directive Principles enforceable by courts? → No
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के संदर्भ में, 'कल्याणकारी राज्य' का विचार निम्नलिखित में से किससे प्रचारित होता है? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 2)

राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व
प्रस्तावना
मौलिक अधिकार
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान में 'कल्याणकारी राज्य' की अवधारणा मुख्यतः राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्वों (भाग IV, अनुच्छेद 36-51) के माध्यम से प्रकट होती है। ये तत्व सरकार को नीतियाँ बनाने और कानून लागू करने का निर्देश देते हैं, जिससे सामाजिक एवं आर्थिक न्याय प्राप्त हो सके। ये गैर-न्यायोच्य हैं, अर्थात अदालतों में लागू नहीं किए जा सकते, परंतु देश के शासन में मूलभूत हैं। इनमें समान कार्य के लिए समान वेतन, शिक्षा का अधिकार, और सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य जैसे प्रावधान शामिल हैं। प्रस्तावना में भी कल्याणकारी राज्य का उल्लेख है, परंतु इसका विस्तृत कार्यान्वयन नीति निदेशक तत्वों के माध्यम से होता है।

question: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution outlines the powers and procedures of the Parliament? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Part VII
Part IV
Part V
Part IX
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Part V

Explanation:
Part V (Articles 52-151) of the Indian Constitution deals with the Union Executive, Legislature, and Judiciary. It specifically outlines the powers, structure, and procedures of the Parliament, including the formation of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, qualifications of members, sessions, legislative process, money bills, joint sittings, and parliamentary committees. This part also covers the President's powers and election, as the President is an integral part of Parliament. Articles 79 to 122 detail parliamentary affairs such as the Speaker and Deputy Speaker, privileges of members, and the procedure for lawmaking. Hence, Part V is the core section defining Parliament's authority and functioning.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which part covers Parliament's powers? → Part V
☛ Article 85 provides for? → Sessions of Parliament
☛ Definition of Money Bill is in? → Article 110
☛ Article 93 deals with? → Election of Lok Sabha Speaker
☛ Parliamentary privileges are in? → Article 105
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का कौन सा भाग संसद की शक्तियों और कार्यप्रणाली को रेखांकित करता है? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: भाग VII
भाग IV
भाग V
भाग IX
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भाग V

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का भाग V (अनुच्छेद 52-151) संघ की कार्यपालिका, विधायिका और न्यायपालिका से संबंधित प्रावधानों को रेखांकित करता है। इसमें संसद की शक्तियों, संरचना, सदस्यों की योग्यता, अधिवेशन, कार्यप्रणाली और विशेषाधिकारों का विस्तृत वर्णन है। भाग V के अंतर्गत लोकसभा और राज्यसभा के गठन, अध्यक्ष एवं उपाध्यक्ष के चुनाव, विधेयकों की प्रक्रिया, धन विधेयक, संयुक्त बैठक और संसदीय समितियों के प्रावधान आते हैं। यह भाग राष्ट्रपति की शक्तियों और उनके पद से जुड़े नियमों को भी सम्मिलित करता है, क्योंकि राष्ट्रपति संसद का अभिन्न अंग है। इस प्रकार, संसद की कार्यप्रणाली और शक्तियों का केंद्र भाग V है।

question: Which of the following fundamental rights is mentioned from Article 25 to Article 28 of the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Right against Exploitation
Right to Equality
Right to Freedom of Religion
Right to Freedom
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Right to Freedom of Religion

Explanation:
Articles 25 to 28 of the Indian Constitution enshrine the Right to Freedom of Religion. This right grants every person the freedom to profess, practice, and propagate any religion of their choice. Article 25 guarantees freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion. Article 26 provides freedom to manage religious affairs. Article 27 prohibits imposition of taxes for promotion of any particular religion. Article 28 ensures freedom from attendance at religious instruction. This right is crucial for maintaining religious harmony and protecting individual faith.

☛ Article 25 → Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion
☛ Article 26 → Freedom to manage religious affairs
☛ Article 27 → Prohibition of taxes for promotion of any religion
☛ Article 28 → Freedom from attendance at religious instruction
☛ Right to Freedom of Religion → Foundation of secularism
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 25 से 28 में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा मौलिक अधिकार उल्लिखित है? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: शोषण के विरुद्ध अधिकार
समानता का अधिकार
धर्म की स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार
स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है धर्म की स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 25 से 28 में धर्म की स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार निहित है। यह अधिकार प्रत्येक व्यक्ति को अपनी पसंद के धर्म को मानने, आचरण करने और प्रचार करने की स्वतंत्रता प्रदान करता है। अनुच्छेद 25 धर्म की अंतःकरण और अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता की गारंटी देता है। अनुच्छेद 26 धार्मिक मामलों के प्रबंधन की स्वतंत्रता देता है। अनुच्छेद 27 किसी विशेष धर्म के प्रचार के लिए कर लगाने पर रोक लगाता है। अनुच्छेद 28 धार्मिक शिक्षा में उपस्थिति की स्वतंत्रता से संबंधित है। यह अधिकार धार्मिक सद्भाव बनाए रखने और व्यक्तिगत आस्था की रक्षा के लिए आवश्यक है।

question: The National Green Tribunals has been established for the enforcement for environmental rights emanating from which Article of the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Article 20
Article 21
Article 22
Article 23
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 21

Explanation:
The National Green Tribunal (NGT) was established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010. It is created for the enforcement of the right to a clean and healthy environment, which emanates from Article 21 (Right to Life) of the Indian Constitution. The Supreme Court has interpreted Article 21 broadly to include the right to environmental protection. NGT ensures speedy disposal of environmental disputes and hears cases related to pollution control. Its chairperson is Justice Prakash Shrivastava, and it has five regional benches.

☛ Who is the chairperson of NGT? → Justice Prakash Shrivastava
☛ How many regional benches does NGT have? → Five
☛ From which Article does NGT enforce environmental rights? → Article 21
☛ Where is the headquarters of NGT? → New Delhi
question_hi: राष्ट्रीय हरित अधिकरण (NGT) भारतीय संविधान के किस अनुच्छेद से उत्पन्न पर्यावरणीय अधिकारों के प्रवर्तन के लिए स्थापित किया गया है? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 2)

question: Which of the following is true about subordinate courts in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: They have independent authority without any oversight from the High Court.
They are directly under the authority of the Supreme Court of India.
They come under the authority of the High Court of the respective state.
They are part of the central judicial system.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is They come under the authority of the High Court of the respective state.

Explanation:
Under Articles 233 to 235 of the Indian Constitution, subordinate courts are placed under the control of the High Court. These courts operate at the district level and include District Judges, Civil Judges, and Magistrates. The High Court has authority over their appointment, transfer, and disciplinary matters. This system ensures judicial uniformity and independence. Therefore, option 3 is correct.

question: Which of the following powers does the Governor NOT possess? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Diplomatic powers
Financial powers
Legislative powers
Executive powers
solution:

Explanation:
The Governor possesses executive, legislative, and financial powers, but does not have diplomatic powers. The Governor is the constitutional head of a state and a representative of the central government. Diplomatic powers, such as making international treaties and managing foreign affairs, are vested with the President of India. The Governor's powers are mainly at the state level, including appointing the Chief Minister, summoning and proroguing the state legislature, and approving money bills. Hence, diplomatic powers are not among the Governor's powers.

question: According to Article 46, the State shall promote the educational and economic interests of: (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: urban populations
weaker sections, particularly Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
all citizens
only women
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is weaker sections, particularly Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes

Explanation:
Article 46 of the Indian Constitution is a Directive Principle of State Policy that directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of weaker sections, especially Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs). It also mandates the State to protect them from social injustice and exploitation. This provision is based on the principles of social justice and equality, reflected in the Preamble and Fundamental Rights. Article 46 is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) in Part IV of the Constitution, which guides the government in policy-making. It was strongly advocated by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar to uplift marginalised communities.

☛ Scheduled Tribes (ST) → Defined under Article 342

question: The Constitution (20th Amendment) Act, 1966, was enacted primarily to address which issue? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: The reorganisation of states based on linguistic lines
The establishment of Panchayati Raj institutions
The validation of appointments and judicial acts of certain district judges
The abolition of the privy purses of erstwhile princely states
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The validation of appointments and judicial acts of certain district judges

Explanation:
The Constitution (20th Amendment) Act, 1966 was enacted primarily to validate the appointments and judicial acts of certain district judges who were not appointed in accordance with Article 233 of the Constitution. This amendment inserted Article 233A, which retrospectively validated their appointments and actions. The need arose when some appointments of district judges were found invalid on technical grounds, threatening the stability of judicial administration. The amendment ensured continuity and legitimacy of judicial decisions made by these judges.

question: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to Comptroller and Auditor General of India? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: He is appointed by the Finance Minister of India.
He is eligible for reappointment.
He is appointed by the Prime Minister of India.
He is appointed by the President of India.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is He is appointed by the President of India.

Explanation:
The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is an independent constitutional authority, appointed by the President through a warrant under his hand and seal. The appointment is made under Article 148 of the Constitution, and the CAG takes an oath before the President. The CAG is not eligible for reappointment, as his term is limited to 6 years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier. The CAG audits the accounts of the Government of India and state governments and submits reports to the President. Neither the Finance Minister nor the Prime Minister can appoint the CAG, as it falls outside their jurisdiction. Thus, the President's sole appointing authority ensures the independence of the CAG.

solution:

This body ensures financial stability and equitable resource allocation among states.

question: Who is responsible for advising the Governor on the formation of the Council of Ministers?  (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 3)

question: How many Fundamental Duties were inserted in the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: 0
11
8
10
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 10

Explanation:
Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. Based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee, a new Part IV-A and Article 51-A were inserted. Initially, there were 10 Fundamental Duties. Later, the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added one more duty (providing educational opportunities to children aged 6-14), making the total 11. However, the question asks about the number inserted by the 42nd Amendment, which was originally 10. These duties remind citizens of their obligations towards the nation and balance the Fundamental Rights.

question: Right to Education is given in _____ of the Indian Constitution.  (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Article 19A
Article 21
Article 21A
Article 24
solution:

Explanation:
Article 21A of the Indian Constitution provides the right to free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14. It was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment (2002) and came into effect in 2010. This right makes education a fundamental right, obligating the state to provide primary education. Under Article 21A, private schools must reserve 25% of seats for economically weaker sections. It is linked to Right to Equality (Article 14) and Right to Life (Article 21).

question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts had added the Ninth Schedule to the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Fifth Constitutional Amendment Act
Ninth Constitutional Amendment Act
Fourth Constitutional Amendment Act
First Constitutional Amendment Act
solution:

Explanation:
The Ninth Schedule was added to the Indian Constitution by the First Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951. This schedule was created to protect land reform and other socio-economic laws from judicial review. Acts included in this schedule cannot be challenged in courts. The First Amendment also added Articles 31A and 31B, and amended Article 19(1)(g). It was passed under the leadership of Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru. Over time, many other laws have been added to the Ninth Schedule.

question: Which of the following do NOT participate in the election of the President of India? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry
Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of states
Nominated members of both Houses of Parliament and Members of Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly
Elected members of both Houses of Parliament
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Nominated members of both Houses of Parliament and Members of Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly

Explanation:
In the election of the President of India, only elected members are eligible to vote. Nominated members of both Houses of Parliament (Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha) do not participate because they are not elected by the people. Members of the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly also do not participate, as Jammu and Kashmir has lost its statehood and is now a Union Territory. In contrast, elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry do participate, as per Article 54 of the Constitution, which includes elected members of state assemblies and both Houses of Parliament. Nominated members are excluded from the electoral college to maintain the principle of direct election by the people's representatives.

☛ Why J&K Assembly members excluded? → Because J&K lost statehood status

question: According to Section 22C(1) of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, Permanent Lok Adalats DO NOT have jurisdiction over disputes related to: (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: non-compoundable offences
compoundable offenses
public utility services
civil disputes
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is non-compoundable offences

Explanation:
According to Section 22C(1) of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, Permanent Lok Adalats have jurisdiction over disputes related to public utility services and civil disputes where the value does not exceed 10 lakh rupees. They also have authority over compoundable offences, which can be settled with the consent of the parties. However, non-compoundable offences such as murder, dacoity, etc., which cannot be compromised, fall outside the jurisdiction of Permanent Lok Adalats. Thus, the correct answer is non-compoundable offences.

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution establishes the Finance Commission as a constitutional body? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 1)

question: In India’s parliamentary system of government, the Prime Minister is regarded as the: (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: De facto executive authority
Ceremonial head of state
Nominal executive authority
Head of the judiciary
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is De facto executive authority

Explanation:
In India's parliamentary system, the President is the ceremonial head of state (De jure executive), while the Prime Minister is the de facto executive authority. The Prime Minister is the head of the Council of Ministers and exercises real executive powers. He is the head of the executive, not the judiciary. According to Articles 74 and 75 of the Constitution, the Prime Minister is appointed by the President and remains in office as long as he enjoys the confidence of the Lok Sabha. Thus, the Prime Minister is regarded as the de facto executive authority.

question_hi: भारत की संसदीय शासन प्रणाली में, प्रधानमंत्री को किस रूप में माना जाता है? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 1)

solution_hi:

Explanation:
भारत की संसदीय शासन प्रणाली में, राष्ट्रपति राज्य का औपचारिक प्रमुख (De jure executive) होता है, जबकि प्रधानमंत्री वास्तविक कार्यकारी अधिकारी (De facto executive) होता है। प्रधानमंत्री मंत्रिपरिषद का प्रमुख होता है और वास्तविक शक्तियों का प्रयोग करता है। वह कार्यपालिका का प्रमुख होता है, न कि न्यायपालिका का। संविधान के अनुच्छेद 74 और 75 के अनुसार, प्रधानमंत्री की नियुक्ति राष्ट्रपति द्वारा की जाती है और वह तब तक पद पर रहता है जब तक उसे लोकसभा का विश्वास प्राप्त है। इस प्रकार, प्रधानमंत्री को वास्तविक कार्यकारी अधिकारी माना जाता है।

question: Who among the following appoints the Speaker Pro Tem of the Lok Sabha? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: The Vice President
The Speaker of the previous Lok Sabha
The President
The Prime Minister
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The President

Explanation:
The Speaker Pro Tem of the Lok Sabha is appointed by the President. This appointment typically takes place before the first session of the newly elected Lok Sabha. The primary duty of the Speaker Pro Tem is to administer oaths to the new members and to oversee the election process for the Speaker. Usually, the most senior member of the House is chosen for this role. This process follows the provisions of the Indian Constitution, which grants certain powers to the President regarding the functioning of the Lok Sabha. The Speaker Pro Tem holds office until a regular Speaker is elected.

question: What is the composition of a Lok Adalat? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: A Lok Adalat consists of a judicial officer and two lawyers.
A Lok Adalat consists of a judicial officer, a lawyer and a social worker.
A Lok Adalat consists of only the judicial officer.
A Lok Adalat consists of a judge and a group of legal experts.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is A Lok Adalat consists of a judicial officer, a lawyer and a social worker.

Explanation:
The composition of a Lok Adalat includes a judicial officer (who can be a retired or sitting judge), a lawyer, and a social worker. This structure is established under the Legal Services Authority Act, 1987. The purpose of a Lok Adalat is to resolve disputes through amicable settlement between the parties. No lawyer is required for either party, and the decision is final and binding on both sides. There is no court fee in Lok Adalat, and if a fee has already been paid, it is refunded. This system provides speedy, inexpensive, and effective justice to the litigants.

☛ How many members are there in a Lok Adalat? → Three members (judicial officer, lawyer, social worker)
☛ What is the nature of a Lok Adalat's decision? → Final and binding
☛ What is the court fee in Lok Adalat? → No fee
☛ What is the main objective of Lok Adalat? → Settlement of disputes through compromise

लोक अदालत की संरचना में एक न्यायिक अधिकारी (जो सेवानिवृत्त या कार्यरत न्यायाधीश हो सकता है), एक वकील और एक सामाजिक कार्यकर्ता शामिल होते हैं। यह व्यवस्था कानूनी सेवा प्राधिकरण अधिनियम, 1987 के तहत की गई है। लोक अदालत का उद्देश्य पक्षकारों के बीच सौहार्दपूर्ण समझौता कराकर विवादों का निपटारा करना है। इसमें किसी भी पक्ष को वकील रखने की आवश्यकता नहीं होती, और फैसला अंतिम होता है तथा दोनों पक्षों पर बाध्यकारी होता है। लोक अदालत में कोर्ट फीस नहीं लगती, और यदि पहले से फीस भरी गई है तो वह वापस कर दी जाती है। यह प्रणाली तेज, सस्ता और प्रभावी न्याय प्रदान करती है।

question: Which body has the constitutional mandate to investigate all matters relating to the safeguards provided for Scheduled Castes under the Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Election Commission of India
National Commission for Minorities
National Commission for Scheduled Castes
National Human Rights Commission
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is National Commission for Scheduled Castes

Explanation:
The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is a constitutional body established under Article 338 of the Indian Constitution. Its primary mandate is to investigate all matters relating to the safeguards provided for Scheduled Castes under the Constitution. The Commission monitors the implementation of these safeguards and submits annual reports to the President and Parliament. The President appoints the Chairperson and other members. Other options like the Election Commission deal with elections, the National Commission for Minorities deals with minorities, and the National Human Rights Commission deals with human rights, but only the National Commission for Scheduled Castes has the constitutional mandate under Article 338 to specifically investigate safeguards for Scheduled Castes.

☛ Who appoints the members of the Commission? → President
☛ What is the main function of the Commission? → To investigate safeguards for Scheduled Castes
☛ Article 338 deals with which body? → National Commission for Scheduled Castes
question_hi: संविधान के तहत अनुसूचित जातियों के लिए प्रदान किए गए सुरक्षा उपायों से संबंधित सभी मामलों की जांच करने का संवैधानिक जनादेश किस निकाय के पास है? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: भारत निर्वाचन आयोग
राष्ट्रीय अल्पसंख्यक आयोग
राष्ट्रीय अनुसूचित जाति आयोग
राष्ट्रीय मानवाधिकार आयोग
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है राष्ट्रीय अनुसूचित जाति आयोग

Explanation:
राष्ट्रीय अनुसूचित जाति आयोग एक संवैधानिक निकाय है जिसका गठन अनुच्छेद 338 के तहत किया गया है। इसका प्रमुख कार्य अनुसूचित जातियों के लिए संविधान में प्रदान किए गए सुरक्षा उपायों की जांच करना और उनके कार्यान्वयन पर निगरानी रखना है। आयोग राष्ट्रपति और संसद को वार्षिक रिपोर्ट प्रस्तुत करता है। इसके अध्यक्ष और अन्य सदस्यों की नियुक्ति राष्ट्रपति द्वारा की जाती है। अन्य विकल्प जैसे निर्वाचन आयोग चुनावों से, अल्पसंख्यक आयोग अल्पसंख्यकों से, और मानवाधिकार आयोग मानवाधिकारों से संबंधित हैं, लेकिन अनुसूचित जातियों के विशेष मामलों की जांच अनुच्छेद 338 के तहत राष्ट्रीय अनुसूचित जाति आयोग का संवैधानिक जनादेश है।
